newsitem.title: USA: Productivity edges up in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Productivity edges up in third quarter.

text.p: U.S. businesses were more efficient in the third quarter of the year, but overall productivity still grew at a slower pace than in the previous quarter, the government said Thursday.
Productivity outside of the agricultural sector rose at a seasonally adjusted 0.2 percent annual rate in the third quarter, after rising 0.5 percent in the second quarter.
The manufacturing sector roared ahead, with productivity jumping 6.3 percent, the biggest gain in two-and-a-half years. Manufacturing provides about 18 percent of the nation's business sector jobs.

Non-farm productivity data provide a reading on the efficiency of business by measuring the amount of goods and services produced per hour by all workers. Growth in productivity allows wages to rise proportionately without accelerating inflation.
Wall Street economists on average had predicted that non-farm productivity would fall 0.1 percent in the third quarter.
Unit labour costs, which make up two-thirds of businesses' production costs, rose at a 3.7 percent rate in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 3.3 percent in the previous month.
For all of last year, productivity rose 0.7 percent following a rise of 0.5 percent in 1994.
